Any LLM OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Pegatron MAAS or a free local model writes the CadQuery program.
PRD + 6 reference photos → a validated STEP solid, plus an STL preview.

Describe the part in a PRD, add a reference photo of each face, and get back a real, validated STEP (`.stp`) solid you can open in Creo, SolidWorks or Fusion — not a render, not a mesh. An LLM (any provider — Pegatron MAAS, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or a free local model on your own machine) drafts a CadQuery program; the server builds it in a sandbox and re-imports the STEP to confirm it is a valid solid before you ever see it.

features.title: Validated output, not eyeballed
features.body: The server re-imports the generated STEP and checks it as a solid (valid bounding box and volume) before returning it.

features.title: Untrusted code, contained
features.body: The model's CadQuery program is AST-guarded (imports allow-listed, dangerous calls blocked) and run in a child process with a hard timeout.

features.title: Parametric and manufacturable
features.body: Output is a BREP solid in millimetres; Creo imports STEP natively, so `.stp` is the interchange deliverable — not a mesh you have to repair.

features.title: Credible authorship
features.body: Built by a working mechanical / aerospace R&D engineer, not a prompt wrapper.

limits: Output is `.stp` (STEP): Creo `.prt` is proprietary and is NOT produced — Creo imports STEP natively, so `.stp` is the interchange deliverable.
Photos are visual reference / dimension assist, not exact geometry: The PRD drives the parametric geometry. This is not a "read the exact shape off six photos" system.
Generated CAD code is untrusted: it is AST-guarded (imports allow-listed, dangerous calls blocked) and run in a child process with a hard timeout. Treat it as untrusted.

ideas.title: Safe by design
ideas.body: A deny-list and fail-closed confirmation before any command runs.

ideas.title: Zero dependencies
ideas.body: Python standard library only, with hermetic tests.

about: A small coding agent that can read a repo, plan, edit files and run tests. The goal is a coding agent used every day, not a Cursor competitor.

steps.title: `.gitignore` matcher
steps.body: a small hand-rolled matcher (no `pathspec`): `#`/blank stripped, `!` negation, trailing `/` dir-only, leading `/` or any internal `/` anchors to the root, a bare pattern matches the basename at any depth, and `*`/`?`/`` wildcards. `SKIP_DIRS` and the `.gitignore` itself are always skipped. A file under an ignored directory is ignored too.

steps.title: `walk`
steps.body: non-ignored file paths only; ignored dirs are pruned so `os.walk` never descends into them.

steps.title: `build_tree`
steps.body: an indented tree built from the file list, so a dir whose contents are all ignored (e.g. `logs/` with only `*.log`) does not appear — like `git ls-files`.

steps.title: `build_context`
steps.body: header + tree, then the most relevant files (task tokens matched in the path weigh more than in the content; smaller files win ties), each capped, up to `budget_chars`.

features.title: Explores, then edits
features.body: Reads the repo, plans, makes minimal edits and runs commands.

features.title: Guardrails on commands
features.body: A command deny-list plus confirmation before anything risky runs.

features.title: Gitignore-aware context
features.body: It reads only what the task needs, respecting your .gitignore.

features.title: Zero dependencies
features.body: HTTP through urllib and JSON through json: nothing to pip install.

features.title: Local and free
features.body: Uses a local Ollama model (qwen3:8b by default) with no API keys; any OpenAI-compatible endpoint also works.

features.title: All milestones done
features.body: M0 to M4 are complete: a working agent you can use today.

limits: Fade can't force anyone to pay, refund or honour a commission: It records what each side confirms (claimed → received) and shows it to both, encrypted. Lightning payments are verified automatically; other methods rely on the receiver confirming.
Card payments go through each person's own PayPal or Stripe: , which charge their usual fees. Fade itself charges nothing and holds nothing.
Public relays don't promise to keep data forever: Fade publishes to 5 relays and caches locally, but a relay may drop old events. Videos on free Blossom hosts can likewise be removed.
Your password is your key: There is no password reset; use a strong password and back up the secret key from Account & privacy.

about: Lingua floats a translated-caption window over Microsoft Teams. It reads the live-caption strip off your screen, OCRs the text, and translates it as the speaker talks, so a mixed-language meeting lands on your screen in your own language.

steps.title: OCR
steps.body: (measured ~0.4 s on the downscaled crop): `POST /chat/completions`, model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR-2`. The caption crop goes in as a base64 `image_url`; the raw caption text comes back in `choices[0].message.content`.

steps.title: Translate
steps.body: (measured 0.3 to 1.0 s): `POST /chat/completions`, an OpenAI-compatible chat call to the configured model with a system prompt that says, in effect, "real-time meeting interpreter; translate into ; output only the translation." A plain (non-streamed) call: the gateway buffers SSE responses, so streaming gained nothing and was dropped.

features.title: Rejected one-call vision
features.body: one-shot vision model

features.title: Region capture
features.body: pick the Teams caption strip once with a drag-a- rectangle picker, then Lingua grabs just that region on a fixed poll interval (default ~900 ms).

features.title: Change detection
features.body: each frame is reduced to a small perceptual hash; when the hash matches the previous frame, Lingua skips OCR and translate entirely, so an idle caption strip costs nothing.

features.title: OCR + translate
features.body: the two MaaS calls above, run on a background worker thread; the UI is never blocked.

features.title: Live-line handling
features.body: the pipeline marks the last (still-growing) line as live so it can be re-translated as more words arrive, and memoises translations so an identical line is never sent to the model twice.

features.title: Light / dark theme
features.body: a toggle in the header switches the whole window, and the choice is saved.

features.title: Live transcript
features.body: target language only (no source text), speaker name on its own line when detected, a scrollbar, and auto-scroll to the newest line unless you have scrolled up.

features.title: Status line
features.body: reports the live OCR and translate latencies.

It combines a Pomodoro timer, looping rain / thunder / brown-noise / café soundscapes, live app-usage tracking, a daily productivity score with a 1–5 star rating, goals / streaks / XP, an hour-of-day focus heatmap, a browsable history log, and a daily AI-style coach + weekly report — all running locally on Windows.

privacy: Focus history is stored locally in `data/productivity.db` (SQLite).

The optional coach LLM and MAAS gateway are used only if configured/enabled. MAAS is off by default in public builds. Keep private configuration private.
The tracker never counts the widget itself as usage, and never counts idle/AFK time toward an app.

about: A device-health copilot for laptops and phones. Cleans storage you can undo, forecasts battery wear and finds what drains your device.
Undoable cleaning Free up space knowing every action can be reversed.

Vitals: a device-health copilot for laptops and phones. It cleans storage you can take back, explains every number it shows, predicts battery wear, catches apps that drain power while you're away, and has a chat that diagnoses problems from plain words ("my laptop is slow", "free 10 GB without touching downloads").

Zero dependencies. The agent runs on the Python 3.8+ standard library (`psutil` is used if it happens to be installed, but nothing needs it), and the front-end is a static offline PWA. It works on macOS, Windows and Linux. On phones it checks the phone itself (storage, memory, battery, heat, uptime in the Android/iPhone app), gives built-in guides, and can pair with your laptop's agent.

privacy: Binds to loopback unless `--lan`. Host-header check (DNS rebinding) and Origin allowlist (drive-by pages).
Every API call except `health`/`pair` needs a session token. Only loopback callers get one automatically; phones need the one-time pairing code (5 wrong tries rotates it).

Cleaning accepts only target ids produced by a scan, never raw paths. The vault also refuses anything outside your home folder, the home root, and standard folders like `~/Documents`, and it never follows symlinks.
Process quit is limited to processes you own that aren't on the protected list, and it sends a normal SIGTERM/taskkill (never force).
limits: Windows and Linux readers and the Windows installer are written against documented APIs, but so far only macOS has been exercised end to end. Windows battery wear needs WMI (`root\wmi`), which some OEMs don't populate.
Automatic-care notifications use `osascript` (macOS), `notify-send` (Linux) or a PowerShell toast (Windows). The Windows path hasn't been tested yet. Set `VITALS_NO_NOTIFY=1` to turn them off.
The browser can't read disk, processes or (in Safari) battery. Browser mode is intentionally partial.
Vitals reads startup items but doesn't disable them. It opens the system settings page instead.
Vault moves are instant on the same volume. Space is released when a batch expires or you purge it.

privacy: No account and no telemetry. Fonts and icons are bundled.
The only external requests go to api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com, and only when you look someone up or open a published brain. Your own brain never leaves your machine.
The local server binds to 127.0.0.1 only, checks the Host header and requires a custom header on every API call.

readme_faq.q: How is it different from Obsidian or Notion?
readme_faq.a: Notion lives in its own cloud, so your repo can't see it. Obsidian is great at linking notes but knows nothing about your project. Cairn keeps everything in the repo as plain files, so it works alongside both and adds the project loop: an ideas wall, a task board, a decision log, a code TODO inbox and a context pack.

readme_faq.q: Does it work with my AI assistant?
readme_faq.a: Yes. The context pack writes brain/CONTEXT.md, a short brief of what's in progress, what's next and which decisions are in force. Point Copilot, Claude, Cursor or ChatGPT at it. No API keys involved.
